> Hi Sofia —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week. Attaching our standard MSA (v3) and the initial Order Form + SOW. We want to move quickly and plan for a production pilot in Q4...

Quick read + plan: I can do a first-pass commercial redline by COB Friday (5 business days is tight given other priority deals but I can prioritize this). If we take our Redwood template as the baseline and produce a marked copy, it will be faster than redlining their counterparty template.

High-level flags I see:
- Data residency: NovoHealth proposes EU/US residency buckets. We should accept multi-region but add Exhibit showing permitted processing locations and a clear fallback for cross-border requests.
- SLA: they ask for 99.95% uptime; recommend we keep standard 99.9% with credits capped per order form. Can discuss for Dedicated if needed.
- IP/outputs: they want a broad license for derivative use — narrow that to use in product for internal features and add constraints on resale.
- Liability cap: push to 12 months' fees or $1M whichever is greater; they propose uncapped exposure for specific indemnities — will need to limit carveouts.

I attached an annotated MSA (MSA_Draft_v3_annotated_by_KPark.docx) with inline comments and three proposed redline options (conservative, compromise, flexible). David — please review the SOW for tokenization and kv-cache hosting notes; I flagged two spots.

Marissa — please confirm preferred billing contact (we will propose net-45 unless procurement asks otherwise).

Aisha — attaching my annotated draft here. If Rebecca prefers tracked changes on their doc, we can do that but it adds time.

Thanks, Kimberly & team — really helpful summary and appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our side after reviewing the annotated draft: 

1) Exhibit for residency: yes, we can accept exhibit-based residency, but need explicit language that pilot data may remain in-region and that production can be migrated under 30 days' notice.
2) SLA / credits: NovoHealth would be willing to accept 99.9% for pilot but requests a 60-day performance review with the ability to request higher SLA for production.
3) IP: our product team asks for broader usage rights for model outputs for derivative model training. Our counsel (Rebecca Turner) is included here — she prefers we exchange tracked changes on the counterparty doc rather than Redwood producing a template redline.

Also: procurement details — procurement@novohealth.com needs a remit-to address and Redwood tax details to draft a PO. Is Marissa the right person to confirm?

We attached a short list of clarifying questions (OrderForm_ClarifyingQs.pdf). If possible, we'd like a short call next week to resolve SLA/residency tradeoffs before final redlines — are you available Tue or Wed morning PST?
